correctness.rationale: Take \(K=2^{-1/2}\begin{pmatrix}1&0\\1&0\end{pmatrix}\), \(a=(e_1+e_2)/\sqrt2\), \(P=P_{e_1}\), the real Hadamard unitary \(U=2^{-1/2}\begin{pmatrix}1&1\\1&-1\end{pmatrix}\), \(Q=\mathrm{diag}(1,-1)\), and \(V=QU\). Direct fresh symbolic multiplication confirms \(K^*K=P\), \(K^\dagger=K^*\), \(KQ=K\), and \(KPU=KPV\), whose identical columns are \(a/\sqrt2\). The frame identity is \(\sum_j|\langle x,f_j\rangle|^2=|\langle x,a\rangle|^2=\|K^*x\|^2\) for every complex \(x\). Yet \(U^*R(K)=\operatorname{span}(e_1)\) while \(V^*R(K)=\operatorname{span}(e_2)\). The frame is literally identical, not merely equivalent. The identity \(T_F^*=U^*PK^*=U^*K^*\) proves the claimed canonical range statement, without proving a substitute bijection.
correctness.risk: The canonical invariant is only claimed choice-independent; no full Grassmannian bijection is established.

value.rationale: The witness invalidates the well-definedness step in a published general \(K\)-frame correspondence even with a fixed ordered Parseval frame, while identifying the invariant range that the frame does canonically determine. This is a motivated, exact correction rather than a generic frame-theory restatement.

final_claim: The Grassmannian map constructed in Sadri--Rahimlou Theorem 3.3 is not well-defined for general closed-range \(K\): one fixed Parseval \(K\)-frame on \(\mathbb C^2\) admits two permitted unitary factorizations giving different lines. The subspace \(R(T_F^*)\), by contrast, is invariant under the choice of unitary.
limitations: Complex dimension two gives one decisive counterexample to the full generality.
No proof that the alternative canonical subspace produces a one-to-one correspondence.
